cases.input:
We just had a pen test finding on one of our internal Flask services (the Orbital Freight dispatch API at dispatch.example.com). The tester got a full table dump through the carrier search endpoint. This is the code they pointed at:

```python
@app.route("/api/carriers/search")
def search_carriers():
    name = request.args.get("name", "")
    region = request.args.get("region", "")
    query = "SELECT id, name, mc_number FROM carriers WHERE name LIKE '%" + name + "%'"
    if region:
        query += " AND region = '" + region + "'"
    cur = db.cursor()
    cur.execute(query)
    return jsonify(cur.fetchall())
```

The fix is easy, but I want a Semgrep rule so we catch this same mistake everywhere else in the monorepo. Can you write one?
cases.expects: A single working Semgrep rule (YAML with id, message, severity, languages, and a pattern) that flags SQL built from request-derived input via string concatenation or formatting and passed to execute, written generally enough to catch f-strings, % and .format variants and other cursor or execute calls, not just this endpoint. Output is the rule itself, not a walkthrough.

A working Semgrep rule for Python that flags yaml.load calls lacking a safe loader (covering both the missing Loader argument and an explicit yaml.Loader or UnsafeLoader) while leaving safe_load and SafeLoader uses unflagged. It is general, not tied to these function names, and the message states the code-execution risk plainly.

cases.input:
From a code review of our agent framework (fictional repo "tool-runner", JS and Python both), the reviewer left this comment and nothing else:

"agent output goes into exec somewhere, and some of the JS side does the same thing with Function. Please make it detectable."

Snippets they pasted:

```python
reply = llm.chat(messages)
code = reply.choices[0].message.content
exec(code)
```

```js
const out = await client.complete({ prompt });
const fn = new Function(out.text);
fn();
```

Not sure which of these they think is the real problem or whether it is one rule or two. Also the Python file also has a harmless exec of a constant string at the top that we do not want flagged. Give me what we should run in CI.
cases.expects: Semgrep rule output that resolves the ambiguity sensibly, most likely a rule for each language (or a clearly valid multi-language approach) that flags model-generated output reaching exec, eval or new Function, ideally using taint tracking or equivalent, and does not flag exec of a constant string. It makes the call without padding with caveats and keeps the rules general rather than matching the pasted variable names.
